reasoning: The genuine claim records the first end and the whole-order end as 1994-06-03. That is the date of EO 12919's signature ('THE WHITE HOUSE, June 3, 1994.'), and nothing in EO 12919 attaches a delayed effective date to section 904. Identity and the one-clause inventory are correct: the order is a single sentence amending sections 303 and 604 of EO 10480, signed September 26, 1991. Section 904(a)(11) supersedes or revokes EO 12773 'except that part of the order that amends section 604 of Executive Order 10480'. Section 904(a)(3) supersedes or revokes EO 10480 itself in the same order. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the amendment lives only as long as its parent, so the section 604 part has no object after 1994-06-03, and both parts end that day. The reasoning is sound. Section 903 keeps prior actions in effect except as inconsistent; the savings statement correctly rests that on EO 12919 rather than on this order. No held order names EO 12773 before EO 12919. The dates, actor, mechanism, quotations and reasons agree with each other and with the sources. Upheld after reveal; the planted version's rejection stands for its altered dates.
